purpose: Turn a finite Composition Contract into a flexible spatial sentence by resolving one subject assembly, one relationship system, one focal operation, one release zone, and one support alignment.
sentence_template: TITLE_MASS + SUBJECT_ASSEMBLY + PRIMARY_RELATION + FOCAL_OPERATION + RELEASE_ZONE + SUPPORT_ALIGNMENT

primitives.role: The dominant reading event and largest coherent typographic mass.
One perceptually unified subject system; it may contain one object, a compact set, a primary with satellites, or one repeated family.
Category, subtitle, and carrier-allowed metadata attached to named structural anchors.
One visibly quieter region with lower contrast, detail, and information density.

global_invariants: Resolve exactly one Composition Contract and one SUBJECT_ASSEMBLY.
Read TITLE_MASS first at thumbnail size even when SUBJECT_MASS occupies more literal canvas area.
Treat object footprint and perceptual attention as separate measurements; a monumental object may be physically larger without becoming the first reading event.
Resolve every visible object into one SUBJECT_MASS. Multiple objects must form one compact silhouette, one primary-subordinate hierarchy, or one repeated path.
Use exactly one focal event and let every energetic secondary element extend it rather than start another event.
Keep exactly one RELEASE_ZONE visibly quieter than the focal event.
Attach SUPPORT_SYSTEM to one shared edge, axis, tangent, frame, mask, vector, rhythm path, or information rule.
Do not distribute several unrelated objects, text blocks, or decorative systems at equal visual weight.

subject_assemblies.count: one coherent subject, object, image field, or abstract field
subject_assemblies.selection_signal: One subject carries the idea, or the source does not explicitly require a relationship among several objects.
subject_assemblies.mass_rule: Treat the single subject as one complete, cropped, fragmented, or field-like mass according to the Composition Contract.

subject_assemblies.selection_signal: The concept depends on a compact ensemble, comparison, toolkit, workstation, or supplied group whose members have comparable semantic importance.
subject_assemblies.mass_rule: Overlap, align, or tightly space 2–3 related objects so their outer silhouette reads as one SUBJECT_MASS before individual parts are noticed.

subject_assemblies.count: one primary object plus one or two subordinate companions
subject_assemblies.selection_signal: One object is clearly primary and one or two accessories, modules, signals, or contextual companions clarify its use or era.
subject_assemblies.mass_rule: Keep the primary object at least twice the visual weight of every satellite; bind satellites to its baseline, axis, tangent, cable, shadow, or directional path.

subject_assemblies.count: two to five instances from one subject family
subject_assemblies.selection_signal: The subject must read as a collection, sequence, inventory, multiplicity, or repeated signal.
subject_assemblies.mass_rule: Repeat one family only; vary scale, crop, angle, or spacing while one instance owns the focal scale and the group follows one coherent path.

operators.definition: Place unequal title and subject masses in complementary regions joined by one shared structural cue.
Organize title, subject, and grounding cue around one calm axial system.
Use one opening, boundary, or threshold to organize entry, enclosure, and title placement.
Place title, subject, and support information on or against one directional or vanishing vector.
Arrange one repeated family along one readable path or controlled grid rhythm.
Let the title control the main field while the physical subject acts only as a subordinate interruption.
Use one recognizable image field and one protected mask or low-detail cut for the title.
Attach title, subject, and truthful factual support to one explicit rule, grid, or index axis.
Enlarge and crop one subject mass decisively at one or more canvas edges.
Make one element intentionally much larger or smaller than expected without creating a second focal event.
Make the title approach, split around, or track one meaningful subject contour while preserving glyph clarity.
Cut one shaped quiet field into the subject or atmospheric mass.
Draw the title or subject toward, through, or across the contract's single opening without adding another portal system.
Create one memorable scale, crop, angle, or spacing variation inside an otherwise coherent repeated path.
Attach at least three major or support elements to one shared edge, axis, baseline, or curvature.
Use one subject tangent as the title or support-copy alignment cue.
Protect one open band or corner from subjects so title and facts remain readable.
Attach support copy to one controlled outer perimeter or frame edge rather than scattering it.

selection_flow.when: The user explicitly requests an assembly
selection_flow.choose: the requested assembly when the Composition Contract and scale role allow it

selection_flow.when: The content explicitly requires repetition, inventory, sequence, or multiplicity
One subject is primary and one or two companions clarify use, function, or era
Two or three related objects form a workstation, toolkit, comparison, or compact ensemble

failure_signals: equal visual weight across multiple objects
support copy floating without a shared structural anchor
object footprint mistaken for perceptual attention
release zone filled with decoration or pseudo-data
